scope: PP4 Prefill (TP1/EP1), one 7988-8064-row microbatch per layer: the post-attention MegaMoE input (residual add, RMSNorm, FP8 group-128 input, router gate GEMM, softmax top-8). Triton sm_90a compile, SASS and Triton-interpreter numerics on CPU only; exactness and speed on H200 are decided in job by scripts/select-firmus-prefill-attention.py (selection moe_input, control = the pinned fused path).

budget_before.source: in-job selection 40883389891 (Decode GPUs, idle clock) and run 40825417205 prefill-0 nsys

hbm_mb_per_layer.post_norm: read o 66 + residual 66, write residual 66 + BF16 y 66 + FP8 x 33

design.idea: y = h * rstd * w with rstd > 0 known only at the end of the row. The FP8 group code of y equals that of h * w under the scale 448 / amax(|h * w|), and the gate logits are rstd * sum_k (h w)_k G_ek. One pass over 64-row tiles of 128 columns writes the residual and the FP8 codes and accumulates the gate GEMM with a BF16 operand BF16(h * w); after the row, the scales and the FP32 logits are multiplied by rstd. The BF16 y is never written or re-read.

numerics.residual: bit-identical (FP32 o + r rounded once to BF16, as the input norm_quant and post_norm_moe_input)
numerics.fp8_input: codes of the unrounded FP32 y (fused rounds y to BF16 first): one rounding fewer
numerics.scales: rstd * amax(|h w|) / 448 in FP32 (fused: amax(|BF16 y|) / 448)
numerics.gate_logits: BF16 operand BF16(h * w) instead of BF16(y), FP32 accumulation, times rstd, rounded to BF16 as the gate GEMM returns them; same operand precision, rounding point moved by the factor rstd
numerics.router: softmax top-8 of the BF16 logits, lowest id on ties, renormalized (the fused-gate router code)
numerics.legality: no coarser format, approximation or skipped work: BF16 operand and FP8 input stay, one BF16 rounding of y is removed

compile.toolchain: Triton 3.6.0 (the version torch 2.11.0 pins) and 3.7.0, sm_90a, cuobjdump from CUDA 13.4; Triton's bundled ptxas 12.8 and TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.4/bin/ptxas
compile.config: BLOCK_M 64, 8 warps, 3 stages, grid 8192 / 64 = 128 programs (125 live at 7988 rows, 1 per SM)
compile.mainloop: HGMMA (wgmma) gate GEMM with the gate weight tile staged by LDGSTS; o/r tiles staged by LDGSTS (cp.async, 3 stages)
compile.why_opaque: With .to(tl.bfloat16) the compiler rematerializes h * w in the MMA operand layout from the staged o/r tiles (duplicate unpack/add/multiply). A non-pure cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 asm (the same RN rounding) makes it move the finished operand through shared memory instead.
compile.scale_ordering: The rstd-free scales are stored inside the loop by the threads that own each row and re-read after the loop in another layout; tl.debug_barrier (BAR.SYNC) separates them. Keeping the 64 x 32 scales in registers instead costs 89 SASS more per group and 203 registers.
compile.issue_estimate: 686 x 8 warps / 4 schedulers = 1372 issue cycles per group per SM against about 2500 cycles of HBM time per group per SM (56 KB at 4.0 TB/s / 126 SMs, 1.42 GHz): memory-bound if the schedulers reach about 0.55 IPC
compile.untouched_kernels: post_norm_moe_input and _gate_route compile to byte-identical SASS before and after the patch (sha256 of the instruction listing, CUDA 13.4 cuobjdump)

cpu_numerics.method: TRITON_INTERPRET=1 with the interpreter's BF16/FP8 conversions and BF16 tl.dot replaced by torch RNE conversions (Triton 3.7 truncates f32->bf16, drops the FP8 mantissa carry and multiplies BF16 bit patterns in tl.dot); the opaque asm is replaced by the identical hw.to(tl.bfloat16). Inputs as the in-job selection draws them (o 0.6, residual 3.0, an all-zero row, a 64x residual row, gate weights 0.02). Run under Triton 3.7.0 and 3.6.0 (numpy 2.2 for the 3.6 interpreter's scalar indexing) with the same results.

expected.onepass_us_per_layer: 58-70 (233 MB at the 4.2-4.3 TB/s the fused post_norm reaches, plus about 3 us of router epilogue)
expected.per_stage_period_ms: 0.82-1.10, central 0.96 for 24 layers (work removal, power-cap factor 1.0); about 0.9 ms after the 5% idle-clock optimism of the in-job timing
expected.launch_gaps: two kernel boundaries (about 5 us per layer) also go; as idle time they return 0.36-0.6x, 0.04-0.07 ms per period
expected.risk: the fused-gate Triton GEMM of 40883389891 read its 66 MB at only about 1.9 TB/s; at that rate onepass would take about 120 us and the selection keeps fused

in_job.where: select-firmus-prefill-attention.py on the four idle Decode GPUs before model load (existing srun, 240 s timeout)
in_job.added_seconds: about 10 (three Triton compiles of about 3 s for onepass and 1-2 s each for post_norm and the router, four gated row counts, two 24-layer graphs x 12 rounds)
